en.title: ⚽ Transition exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ Transition exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on the defensive transition (pressing and quick recovery run).

Attack-to-defence transitions.

Play starts with a sprint by a player who shoots at the big goal.

As soon as he shoots, a player (light blue here) comes in and plays a 1 against 1.

The player who shot has to defend and can score in two mini goals if he wins the ball.

At the end of the action, two players (in red here) come in to attack 2v2 against the two players already in play (the shooter and the light-blue player).

Then four players (in yellow here) arrive to play a 4v4 against the four players already in play.

Each attacking team has 15 seconds to score in the big goal.

The transitions are immediate between each sequence.

At the end of the 4v4, the roles change and a new shooting player sets off.

The drill works on reaction speed and transition reflexes.

It also rewards getting back into defensive shape and reacting to the loss.

Duration: short, intense 2-minute sequences with rotation.

en.title: ⚽ Transition exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ Transition exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on the fast counter-attack after winning the ball back.

Offensive transition – Fast counter-attack.

A large area is set up in the middle of the pitch for a 4 against 3.

An area near the opponents' box holds a 2 against 2.

The team in possession keeps the ball in the central rectangle.

It has to complete 10 passes to score a point.

The other team presses. When it wins the ball, it plays forward immediately and has to pass to the 2 players in the area near the penalty area.

The players have to move quickly to exploit the spaces.

Offside applies from the forward pass onwards, to organise the defence. The drill develops speed of execution, playing forward and fast decision-making.

Do 6 sequences of 2 minutes each.

At each sequence, change the roles so that all the teams alternate possession, winning the ball and counter-attacking.

en.title: ⚽ Transition exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ Transition exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on the build-up attack and taking the initiative.

Build-up attack or fast transition – 8 against 8 + 2 jokers. Play takes place on 2/3 of a pitch, with the big goals and two goalkeepers.

Two teams of 8 play against each other, helped by 2 jokers placed on the sides.

The team in possession has to complete 10 passes before it can shoot at goal.

The jokers act as outside outlets to make the circulation easier.

If the other team wins the ball, it can launch an immediate offensive transition.

Two options: attack quickly on the counter, or slow it down for a build-up attack.

The coach sometimes stops play to question the players.

Question: should you have played fast or slowed it down?

A bonus point is awarded if the decision taken is judged to be right.

Aim: develop efficiency in the build-up attack and clear thinking in transition.

en.caption_fb:
⚽ Speed exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on sharpness, agility and coordination.

The “Pac-Man” game.

Mark out lines (with cones for example) on half a pitch (or an area suited to the number of players available).

With 16 players for example: 12 players “on the run”.

3-4 Pac-Men (here in red) who have to touch the players on the run.

The players must always run along a line, as in the Pac-Man game.

A player who is touched becomes a Pac-Man.

Duration suited to the level and the objective.

en.caption_fb:
⚽ Speed exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on speed with the ball and decision-making.

Put out 4 cones of different colours.

The coach calls out 2 colours (here yellow and green).

The player has to react quickly to the signal, go round the 2 cones of the colours called then take the ball and score.

Team competition.

The player who touches the ball first scores 3 points.

The player who scores gets 2 points.

Recovery 45 seconds minimum.

4 to 6 repetitions for example.

To be done in the first part of the session.

en.title: ⚽ Speed exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ Speed exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on reaction speed and sharpness.

The players set off sprinting, then in full stride the coach calls out a colour (he calls out a colour whenever he wants, at any moment of the players' run).

The players go off on the side of the colour called (here blue or red) and have to get the ball and score.

The coach can call out the colour or show a coloured cone.

He can also move while the players are running.

So the players have to follow the coach's movement while they run to take in the information.

en.title: ⚽ Speed exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ Speed exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on reaction speed and sharpness, with concentration.

Reaction speed.

Form two teams facing each other; each player has a number.

A central square is marked out on the ground as a noughts and crosses grid (3x3).

On the coach's signal, a number is called.

The players concerned sprint immediately towards the square.

Each player has to stand in a free cell of the grid.

The coach then calls a new number, and so on.

The aim is to make a line of 3 players:

horizontal, vertical or diagonal.

The exercise is done over 5-6 repetitions for example. 30 seconds of recovery minimum between 2 goes.

Possible variations: vary the distances, add obstacles, impose a type of movement, etc.

A fun exercise combining speed, thinking and competition.

⚽ Speed exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on sharpness, agility and coordination.

Sharpness, agility and decision-making work.

Form 2 teams.

Set up a grid on the ground (the “four in a row” game).

The players go as a relay.

On the coach's signal, a player sets off:

he does a short course (hurdles, poles, slalom…), goes and takes a cone in his colour then heads for the grid.

The player puts a cone in a free cell.

Quick return to let the next player go.

Aim: make a line of 4 (horizontal, vertical or diagonal).

Work as a dynamic and competitive relay.

4-5 times for example.

Recovery 45 seconds between each go.

en.title: ⚽ Speed exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ Speed exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on sharpness, agility and coordination.

Reaction and agility (mirror).

2 players are linked by a rope.

Each end is simply tucked into the shorts, never tied around the waist: the rope must be able to come loose.

One of the two players (named before the start) has to get the rope to come away by feinting to his right or to his left (going backwards or forwards is not allowed).

The other player has to react immediately and follow the movements to keep the rope taut.

Work in short and intense sequences.

Swap the roles at each go.

2-3 times in both roles, 45 seconds of recovery between two goes.

en.title: ⚽ Speed exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ Speed exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on speed with the ball and decision-making.

3v2 after speed work, on half a pitch with a goal and a goalkeeper.

The 3 attackers (in blue) start from the corner, on the goal line. The 2 defenders (in yellow) start from flat marker 2, on the other touchline, level with the halfway line.

The coach stands near the centre circle with the balls.

On the signal, the attackers do a short there-and-back (5 m), then sprint along the touchline to the pole on the halfway line and go around it: the coach passes the ball to one of them.

On the same signal, the defenders do a there-and-back between flat markers 2 and 1 (about 10 m), then sprint along the touchline to flat marker 3, level with the goal line, and enter the box to defend.

The attackers have 10 seconds to score from the coach's pass.

On a full-size pitch, move the pole and flat markers 1 and 2 forward to 25-30 m from goal: the run before the opposition must remain a sprint of 5 to 6 seconds.

3 goes in each role, 2 minutes of recovery between 2 goes (walking back).

en.title: ⚽ HIIT exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ HIIT exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on the ability to string together intense duels (1 against 1), with interval work.

1v1.

Intervals: 30 seconds of play, 1 minute of recovery for example (beyond 20 to 30 seconds, the quality of the duel often drops).

As a mini-tournament (promotion and relegation) with the games changing.

The winners move up to finish on pitch 1.

Pitch 4: possession (the player who keeps the ball longest wins).

Pitch 3: stop ball in the red zone.

Pitch 2: the player has to go between the opponent's flat markers (red or blue).

Pitch 1: score in the opponent's mini goal.

The intensity has to be high. 8 games for example.

en.title: ⚽ Transition exercise
en.caption_fb:
⚽ Transition exercise

🎯 Objective: Work on the fast counter-attack after winning the ball back.

Counter-attack after a goal is scored.

Two teams of 6 players, with two goalkeepers.

Play is a free game on half a pitch.

When a team scores, two of its players have to go round the markers placed near the opponents' goal immediately.

Meanwhile, the team that has just conceded can play out quickly with a numerical advantage (6 against 4).

That simulates an immediate counter-attack after a favourable transition.

The team a man down has to get back into position quickly and defend in an emergency.

Attacking aim: exploit the numerical advantage by going straight for goal.

Defensive aim: communication, sliding across and slowing the play down to buy time. Each sequence restarts as soon as an action is over.

Play two times 6 minutes with 2 minutes of recovery.

Focus: offensive transition speed, fast defensive reorganisation.

→ More exercises and programmes: www.ppf11.com/en/
